he: ויוכל למצא אחד שעל ידי חכמתו ודעתו יאמר סברא שאינה אמתית, שיתגלגל על ידי זה שיבואו להתיר חס ושלום אסור כזה חמשה לאוין בתורה, ולחזק על ידי זה עוברי עברה. אשר ראוי לכל מחבר ספר לצעק על זה בכל מיני קולות, וצעקת שבר יעורר על פרצה הזאת שנעשה בישראל זה קרוב במדינות אשכנז לעבר בכל יום חמשה לאוין. כי גם במדינות אשכנז אין המנהג הרע הזה מימות עולם חס ושלום, רק הרבה יותר מאלף שנים אחר חרבן בית שני התחילה הרעה הגדולה הזאת לצמח בהם. כי שמעתי מרבנו זכרונו לברכה שגם אמות העולם לא היו מגלחים זקנם בימי קדם וזה סמוך איזה מאות שנים שהתחילו אמות העולם לגלח זקנם, ואחר כך בזמן רב בתקף מרירות הגלות התפשטה הסטרא אחרא והתגרה היצר הרע גם בבני ישראל ונתערבו בגויים ולמדו ממעשיהם והתחילו איזה רשעים גדולים מפרסמים לגלח זקנם, וכן למדו אחד מחברו עד שנתרבה הפרצה בעוונותינו הרבים ונעשה להם כהתר, כאשר רואים גם עכשו שהכשרים באמת אינם מגלחים זקנם גם באשכנז.
he_nikud: וְיוּכַל לִמְצֹא אֶחָד שֶׁעַל־יְדֵי חָכְמָתוֹ וְדַעְתּוֹ יֹאמַר סְבָרָא שֶׁאֵינָהּ אֲמִתִּית, שֶׁיִּתְגַּלְגֵּל עַל־יְדֵי־זֶה שֶׁיָּבוֹאוּ לְהַתִּיר חַס וְשָׁלוֹם אִסּוּר כָּזֶה חֲמִשָּׁה לָאוִין בַּתּוֹרָה, וּלְחַזֵּק עַל־יְדֵי־זֶה עוֹבְרֵי עֲבֵרָה. אֲשֶׁר רָאוּי לְכָל מְחַבֵּר סֵפֶר לִצְעֹק עַל־זֶה בְכָל מִינֵי קוֹלוֹת, וְצַעֲקַת שֶׁבֶר יְעוֹרֵר עַל פִּרְצָה הַזֹּאת שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל זֶה קָרוֹב בִּמְדִינוֹת אַשְׁכְּנַז לַעֲבֹר בְּכָל יוֹם חֲמִשָּׁה לָאוִין. כִּי גַּם בִּמְדִינוֹת אַשְׁכְּנַז אֵין הַמִּנְהָג הָרָע הַזֶּה מִימוֹת עוֹלָם חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, רַק הַרְבֵּה יוֹתֵר מֵאֶלֶף שָׁנִים אַחַר חֻרְבַּן בַּיִת שֵׁנִי הִתְחִילָה הָרָעָה הַגְּדוֹלָה הַזֹּאת לִצְמֹחַ בָּהֶם. כִּי שָׁמַעְתִּי מֵרַבֵּנוּ זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה שֶׁגַּם אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם לֹא הָיוּ מְגַלְּחִים זְקָנָם בִּימֵי קֶדֶם וְזֶה סָמוּךְ אֵיזֶה מֵאוֹת שָׁנִים שֶׁהִתְחִילוּ אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם לְגַלֵּחַ זְקָנָם, וְאַחַר־כָּךְ בִּזְמַן רַב בְּתֹקֶף מְרִירוּת הַגָּלוּת הִתְפַּשְּׁטָה הַסִּטְרָא־אָחֳרָא וְהִתְגָּרָה הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע גַּם בִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְנִתְעָרְבוּ בַּגּוֹיִים וְלָמְדוּ מִמַּעֲשֵׂיהֶם וְהִתְחִילוּ אֵיזֶה רְשָׁעִים גְּדוֹלִים מְפֻרְסָמִים לְגַלֵּחַ זְקָנָם, וְכֵן לָמְדוּ אֶחָד מֵחֲבֵרוֹ עַד שֶׁנִּתְרַבָּה הַפִּרְצָה בַּעֲווֹנוֹתֵינוּ הָרַבִּים וְנַעֲשָׂה לָהֶם כְּהֶתֵּר, כַּאֲשֶׁר רוֹאִים גַּם עַכְשָׁו שֶׁהַכְּשֵׁרִים בֶּאֱמֶת אֵינָם מְגַלְּחִים זְקָנָם גַּם בְּאַשְׁכְּנַז.
en: And one may find someone who, through his wisdom and knowledge, will state a line of reasoning that is not true, so that through this it will come about that they will come to permit, Heaven forbid, such a prohibition—five prohibitions in the Torah—and thereby strengthen transgressors. Every author of a book ought to cry out about this with all kinds of voices, and raise a cry of anguish over this breach that has recently been made in Israel in the countries of Ashkenaz, to transgress five prohibitions every day. For even in the countries of Ashkenaz this evil custom has not existed from time immemorial, Heaven forbid; rather, it was much more than a thousand years after the destruction of the Second Temple that this great evil began to spring up among them. For I heard from our Rabbi, of blessed memory, that even the nations of the world did not shave their beards in ancient days, and it is only some hundreds of years since the nations of the world began to shave their beards; and afterward, a long time later, amid the intense bitterness of exile, the sitra achra [other side] spread and the evil inclination incited even the children of Israel, and they mingled among the nations and learned from their deeds, and some notorious, very wicked men began to shave their beards; and thus one learned from another, until the breach increased, through our many sins, and it became as though permitted to them, as one sees even now, that those who are truly upright do not shave their beards, even in Ashkenaz.

he: וגם במדינות הסמוכים לאשכנז עדין לא נתפשטה הרעה הזאת כמו באשכנז, רק כי הרשעים הגדולים מתחילים בזה, ואחר כך טועים בזה גם הכשרים קצת. וגם עתה כשמוכיחים אותם שעוברים על חמשה לאוין בתורה, הם עונין שמגלחין על ידי סם שמתר באמת, ומי שנוהג כן יש לו התר על פי הדין ולא על פי כתבי האר"י זכרונו לברכה וזהר הקדוש. אבל בוחן לבות יודע שרבם עוברים במזיד ומגלחים בשאט נפש בידים בתער, ומאחר שהם בעצמם מודים שבתער אסור, כי אינם יכולים להכחיש המפרש בתורה ובגמרא והם בעצמם בנפשם יודעים האמת אם מגלחים בתער או בסם, כמה יש לבכות ולצעק במר נפש ולבכות כנחל שוטף מאין הפוגות על הפרצה הזאת אשר נעשה בישראל. עד שהתחילה לצמח הרעה הזאת סמוך למדינתנו שנמצאים גם שם רשעים כאלו הפורקים על ומגלחים זקנם. השם יתברך ירחם על פלטת עמו ויציל הפלטה הנשארת בכחו הגדול והנורא ויביא לנו משיח צדקנו ויגלה האמת בעולם במהרה בימינו אמן:
he_nikud: וְגַם בַּמְּדִינוֹת הַסְּמוּכִים לְאַשְׁכְּנַז עֲדַיִן לֹא נִתְפַּשְּׁטָה הָרָעָה הַזֹּאת כְּמוֹ בְּאַשְׁכְּנַז, רַק כִּי הָרְשָׁעִים הַגְּדוֹלִים מַתְחִילִים בָּזֶה, וְאַחַר־כָּךְ טוֹעִים בָּזֶה גַּם הַכְּשֵׁרִים קְצָת. וְגַם עַתָּה כְּשֶׁמּוֹכִיחִים אוֹתָם שֶׁעוֹבְרִים עַל חֲמִשָּׁה לָאוִין בַּתּוֹרָה, הֵם עוֹנִין שֶׁמְּגַלְּחִין עַל־יְדֵי סַם שֶׁמֻּתָּר בֶּאֱמֶת, וּמִי שֶׁנּוֹהֵג כֵּן יֵשׁ לוֹ הֶתֵּר עַל־פִּי הַדִּין וְלֹא עַל־פִּי כִּתְבֵי הָאַרִ"י זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה וְזֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ. אֲבָל בּוֹחֵן לִבּוֹת יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁרֻבָּם עוֹבְרִים בְּמֵזִיד וּמְגַלְּחִים בִּשְׁאָט נֶפֶשׁ בְּיָדַיִם בְּתַעַר, וּמֵאַחַר שֶׁהֵם בְּעַצְמָם מוֹדִים שֶׁבְּתַעַר אָסוּר, כִּי אֵינָם יְכוֹלִים לְהַכְחִישׁ הַמְפֹרָשׁ בַּתּוֹרָה וּבַגְּמָרָא וְהֵם בְּעַצְמָם בְּנַפְשָׁם יוֹדְעִים הָאֱמֶת אִם מְגַלְּחִים בְּתַעַר אוֹ בְּסַם, כַּמָּה יֵשׁ לִבְכּוֹת וְלִצְעֹק בְּמַר נֶפֶשׁ וְלִבְכּוֹת כְּנַחַל שׁוֹטֵף מֵאֵין הֲפוּגוֹת עַל הַפִּרְצָה הַזֹּאת אֲשֶׁר נַעֲשָׂה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל. עַד שֶׁהִתְחִילָה לִצְמֹחַ הָרָעָה הַזֹּאת סָמוּךְ לִמְדִינָתֵנוּ שֶׁנִּמְצָאִים גַּם שָׁם רְשָׁעִים כָּאֵלּוּ הַפּוֹרְקִים עֹל וּמְגַלְּחִים זְקָנָם. הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יְרַחֵם עַל פְּלֵטַת עַמּוֹ וְיַצִּיל הַפְּלֵטָה הַנִּשְׁאֶרֶת בְּכֹחוֹ הַגָּדוֹל וְהַנּוֹרָא וְיָבִיא לָנוּ מְשִׁיחַ צִדְקֵנוּ וִיגַלֶּה הָאֱמֶת בָּעוֹלָם בִּמְהֵרָה בְיָמֵינוּ אָמֵן:
en: And even in the countries adjoining Ashkenaz this evil has not yet spread as it has in Ashkenaz; it is only that the greatly wicked begin this, and afterward even the somewhat upright err in this. And even now, when they are reproved for transgressing five prohibitions in the Torah, they answer that they shave by means of a depilatory substance, which is indeed permitted; and one who acts thus has permission according to the law, but not according to the writings of the Ari, of blessed memory, and the holy Zohar. But the One who examines hearts knows that most of them transgress deliberately and shave defiantly, by direct action, with a razor; and since they themselves admit that [shaving] with a razor is forbidden, for they cannot deny what is explicit in the Torah and the Gemara, and they themselves know in their own souls the truth, whether they shave with a razor or with a depilatory substance, how much one must weep and cry out in bitterness of soul, and weep like a rushing stream without respite, over this breach that has been made in Israel! To the point that this evil has begun to spring up near our country, where such wicked men are also found, casting off the yoke and shaving their beards. May Hashem, blessed be He, have mercy upon the remnant of His people and save the remnant that remains, by His great and awesome power, and bring us our righteous Messiah and reveal the truth in the world speedily in our days, amen.

he: (נב) קדם שאמר רבנו זכרונו לברכה התורה הנדפסת בלקוטי תנינא בסימן ל"ב המתחלת יש צדיקים גנוזים, ונאמרה בשבת פרשת יתרו תקס"ט לפ"ק [לפרט קטן]. וספר מעשה מקדם שהבעל שם טוב זכרונו לברכה היה בקהלת קדש בראד ונתאכסן אצל גביר אחד והיו מסבין שם על השלחן אנשים רבים מכבדים לכבודו כנהוג, והיה יושב שם למטה אצל השלחן בעל דרשיר אחד הינו דרשן. והיה אוכל הרבה, והסתכלו עליו שאוכל הרבה מאד, והתחילו לתן לו ולהושיט לו אכילה הרבה בשביל ליצנות. והדרשן עשה את שלו, ואכל הרבה כל מה שהושיטו לו כגון דגים שהיו אוכלים שני אנשים חתיכה אחת והדרשן אכל בעצמו שתי חתיכות דגים, וכן רטב שהיה אוכל בעצמו קערה מלאה וכן בשאר המאכלים והם הושיטו לו בכל פעם בשביל ליצנות מחמת שראו שאוכל הרבה.
he_nikud: נב) קֹדֶם שֶׁאָמַר רַבֵּנוּ זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה הַתּוֹרָה הַנִּדְפֶּסֶת בְּלִקּוּטֵי תִּנְיָנָא בְּסִימָן ל"ב הַמַּתְחֶלֶת יֵשׁ צַדִּיקִים גְּנוּזִים, וְנֶאֶמְרָה בְּשַׁבָּת פָּרָשַׁת יִתְרוֹ תקס"ט לפ"ק [לִפְרָט קָטָן]. וְסִפֵּר מַעֲשֶׂה מִקֹּדֶם שֶׁהַבַּעַל־שֵׁם־טוֹב זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה הָיָה בִּקְהִלַּת־קֹדֶשׁ בְּרָאד וְנִתְאַכְסֵן אֵצֶל גְּבִיר אֶחָד וְהָיוּ מְסֻבִּין שָׁם עַל הַשֻּׁלְחָן אֲנָשִׁים רַבִּים מְכֻבָּדִים לִכְבוֹדוֹ כַּנָּהוּג, וְהָיָה יוֹשֵׁב שָׁם לְמַטָּה אֵצֶל הַשֻּׁלְחָן בַּעַל דַּרְשֶׁיר אֶחָד הַיְנוּ דַּרְשָׁן. וְהָיָה אוֹכֵל הַרְבֵּה, וְהִסְתַּכְּלוּ עָלָיו שֶׁאוֹכֵל הַרְבֵּה מְאֹד, וְהִתְחִילוּ לִתֵּן לוֹ וּלְהוֹשִׁיט לוֹ אֲכִילָה הַרְבֵּה בִּשְׁבִיל לֵיצָנוּת. וְהַדַּרְשָׁן עָשָׂה אֶת שֶׁלּוֹ, וְאָכַל הַרְבֵּה כָּל מַה שֶּׁהוֹשִׁיטוּ לוֹ כְּגוֹן דָּגִים שֶׁהָיוּ אוֹכְלִים שְׁנֵי אֲנָשִׁים חֲתִיכָה אַחַת וְהַדַּרְשָׁן אָכַל בְּעַצְמוֹ שְׁתֵּי חֲתִיכוֹת דָּגִים, וְכֵן רֹטֶב שֶׁהָיָה אוֹכֵל בְּעַצְמוֹ קְעָרָה מְלֵאָה וְכֵן בִּשְׁאָר הַמַּאֲכָלִים וְהֵם הוֹשִׁיטוּ לוֹ בְּכָל פַּעַם בִּשְׁבִיל לֵיצָנוּת מֵחֲמַת שֶׁרָאוּ שֶׁאוֹכֵל הַרְבֵּה.
en: (52.) Before Rabbainu, of blessed memory, said the Torah printed in Likutay Tinyana, section 32, which begins "There are hidden tzaddikim," and was said on the Sabbath of the Torah portion Yisro, 5569, le-frat katan [minor era]—he related a story from earlier times: the Baal Shem Tov, of blessed memory, was in the holy community of Brod and lodged with a certain wealthy man, and many distinguished people were reclining there at the table in his honor, as is customary. And sitting there lower down at the table was a certain baal darshir, that is, a preacher. And he was eating much, and they watched him eating very much, and began to give him and to hand him much food for mockery. And the preacher went on with what he was doing and ate much, everything that they handed him—such as fish: two people would eat one piece, while the preacher ate two pieces of fish by himself; and likewise broth, of which he would eat a full bowl by himself, and likewise with the other foods. And they handed him [food] each time for mockery, because they saw that he ate much.

editorial_apparatus.text: 52.179.1: Both Hebrew fields name Likutay Tinyana and section ל"ב; tzaddikim means righteous persons. The pointed opening lacks the unpointed opening parenthesis; both exact witnesses are retained. Supplied pointing is evidence, not proof of authorial priority.

52.179.2: תקס"ט לפ"ק [לפרט קטן] is preserved as the Hebrew-year designation with its explicit abbreviation/gloss; the conventional millennium is supplied in 5569. The secondary Gregorian [1809] is not in either Hebrew witness and is removed, not used to resolve the date.

52.179.3: Independent review supersedes the initial preference for first/beforehand. וספר מעשה מקדם / וְסִפֵּר מַעֲשֶׂה מִקֹּדֶם is selected as he related a story from earlier times; alternatively, he related the story beforehand, before the Torah. Word order favors attaching מקדם to מעשה, but the supplied pointing does not settle attachment or prove authorial priority. No separate date for the Baal Shem Tov episode is inferred. בראד / בְּרָאד remains Brod; wealthy host, many distinguished reclining guests, honor and custom are preserved.
52.179.4: בעל דרשיר / בַּעַל דַּרְשֶׁיר is retained as baal darshir with the source’s own הינו דרשן gloss; למטה means lower down, without asserting a precise seating plan.

52.179.4.IR: The supplied pointing בַּעַל דַּרְשֶׁיר suggests a dar-sheir/dar-sher vocalization, while the unpointed witness is בעל דרשיר; baal darshir is retained as a conventional transliteration, not an authenticated etymology. The secure semantic basis is the source’s own הינו דרשן / הַיְנוּ דַּרְשָׁן (that is, a preacher).

52.179.5: Both witnesses repeat much/very much/much and distinguish giving from handing (לתן לו ולהושיט לו / לִתֵּן לוֹ וּלְהוֹשִׁיט לוֹ). Independent review selects hand rather than offer for the physical action. בשביל ליצנות / בִּשְׁבִיל לֵיצָנוּת is intentional mockery, not merely a benign joke. Ongoing eating and the guests’ beginning to act are retained.
52.179.6: עשה את שלו is rendered idiomatically as went on with what he was doing, without adding praise or blame. הרבה and כל are both retained.
52.179.7: Both fields specify two people sharing one piece versus the preacher alone eating two pieces of fish. Repeated fish and the numerical contrast remain explicit.

52.179.8: רטב / רֹטֶב may denote sauce, gravy or broth; broth is a provisional contextual choice, not a claim that the pointing establishes soup. Both likewise repetitions and the full bowl eaten alone are retained.

52.179.9: [Food] supplies the implicit object only. והם הושיטו לו / וְהֵם הוֹשִׁיטוּ לוֹ is now rendered And they handed him; the renewed guests’ agency, each time, repeated mockery and causal reason remain separate from the earlier account.

translationSourceEnglish: (52.) Before Rabbainu o.b.m. said the Torah printed in Likutay Moharan, vol. 2, Torah 32 — which begins "There are hidden tzaddikim," and was said on the Sabbath of the Torah portion Yisro, 5569 [1809] in the minor era — he told the following story: The Baal Shem Tov o.b.m. was once in the holy community of Brod, and was lodging by a certain wealthy man, and many distinguished people were reclining there at the table in his honor as is customary. he_nikud: נג) תקס"ח סָמוּךְ לְרֹאשׁ־הַשָּׁנָה נָסַעְנוּ עִמּוֹ מִחוּץ לָעִיר אֲנִי וַחֲבֵרִי רַבִּי נַפְתָּלִי, וְסִפֵּר שֶׁחָלַם לוֹ בַּאֲשֶׁר שֶׁהָיוּ מְשִׂיחִים שֶׁהָרְפוּאָה הִיא מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְבַד כִּי אֲנִי ה' רוֹפְאֶךָ. וְרַק הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יָכוֹל לְרַפְּאוֹת וְאָמְרוּ מִי יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ רוֹצֶה וְעָנָה אֶחָד מִשְּׁנֵינוּ וְלֹא רָצָה לְהַגִּיד מִי הָאֶחָד כִּ'י אֲ'נִי ה' ר'וֹפְאֶךָ מוֹרֶה עַל־זֶה כִּי הוּא רָאשֵׁי־תֵבוֹת אָ'מֵן כֵּ'ן יְ'הִי רָ'צוֹן כַּנִּדְפַּס בְּלִקּוּטֵי תִּנְיָנָא סִימָן מ"ב:
en: (53.) In 5568, close to Rosh Hashana, we traveled with him outside the city, I and my companion Rabbi Naftoli. And he related that he had dreamed that they were conversing that healing is from Hashem, blessed be He, alone, for "I am Hashem your healer." And only Hashem, blessed be He, can heal. en: (54) He spoke with us concerning the Torah printed in Likutey Tinyana, section 40, which begins: One who knows of the Land of Israel, who has truly tasted the taste of the Land of Israel, and said that he had known this long before, for, after all, I traveled to the Land of Israel, and presumably I had previously had a desire and yearning to travel to the Land of Israel, and I also dreamed of the Land of Israel. And once a certain man was with me, and I spoke with him, and a great yearning and desire for the Land of Israel began to awaken within me. And afterward I asked him whether he had been with tzaddikim on Rosh Hashana, and he told me that he had been with several great, true tzaddikim on Rosh Hashana, and because of this I had great yearning when I spoke with him, as explained in the aforementioned Torah.

en: (55) And likewise, the matter of the twenty-four kinds of pidyonos (redemptions) needed to sweeten the twenty-four courts of judgment, printed in Likutey I, section 215—he already knew of this before he was in the Land of Israel. As I heard from our fellowship, and particularly from one distinguished man of our fellowship, who related that once his wife became ill and was literally close to death; her soul had almost departed. And he came to him, of blessed memory, and [the latter] said to him: Run quickly and bring twenty-four pidyonos before the verdict is decreed and sealed. And he ran and brought him a sack full of money. And afterward a miracle occurred and she returned to her health, and afterward our Rabbi, of blessed memory, commanded that all the money be returned to him, only to accept twenty-four gedolim [a type of coin] and distribute them to the poor.

he: ואז דבר גם כן שאי אפשר לעשות פדיון כי אם כשיודעין כל העשרים וארבעה מיני פדיונות להמתיק כל העשרים וארבעה בתי דינים. ואמר משל כמו כשתובעין אחד בגובערני [ממשל] של קיעב והוא מעמיד טוען שקורין פיליפטענט בקאמיניץ. כך איך אפשר לעשות פדיון אם אינו יודע באיזה בתי דינין דנין אותו.

en: And then he also spoke of how it is impossible to perform a pidyon except when one knows all twenty-four kinds of pidyonos, to sweeten all twenty-four courts of judgment. And he gave a parable: as when a claim is brought against someone in the guberniye [government] of Kiev, and he appoints an advocate, called a filiptent, in Kaminitz. Thus, how is it possible to perform a pidyon if one does not know in which courts of judgment they are judging him?

en: And he also said then that there is a pidyon so exalted that it can sweeten all twenty-four courts of judgment, and there are several further conversations about this from earlier, but he did not then know the entire matter in its completeness as he knew it afterward, as he revealed a little of this to us: that sometimes, even with this pidyon which encompasses all twenty-four courts of judgment, it nevertheless does not avail, because a different matter comes about from this, namely converts, and this is the aspect of Moses, who stands between shmad (apostasy) and ratzon (favor). All this he did not know then, but only afterward, through his service, in which he toiled and labored at all times until each time he reached higher, more exalted levels; and then he attained and understood, in wondrous revelation, what he had known at first in an unspecified way, in an aspect of concealment, only by allusion.

translationSourceEnglish: And he also said then that there is a pidyon so elevated that it can sweeten all twenty-four courts of law. And there are in this matter many additional conversations from before — but he did not then know the entire matter in its completeness as he knew it afterwards. For then he knew only this: that sometimes even this pidyon that encompasses all twenty-four courts of law is nevertheless insufficient, because through it a different matter arises — namely, converts — and this is the aspect of Moses who stands between apostasy and [Divine] favor. All this he did not know then — only afterwards, through his service [of G‑d] in which he toiled and labored at all times, until he arrived each time at ever higher and more exalted levels — he then attained and understood in a wondrous revelation what he had previously known vaguely, in a hidden way, only by allusion.

he: ומזה תוכל להבין מעט מקצת גדלתו כי גם מקדם היה חדוש נפלא חד בדרא, כי אמר שמאלו העשרים וארבעה פדיונות אינו יודע כי אם חד בדרא. וכל זה היה קדם ארץ ישראל ואחר כך כשבא מארץ ישראל אמר שהוא מתביש בכל התורות וההשגות שהשיג קדם שהיה בארץ ישראל ולא היו נחשבים בעיניו לכלום. ראה והבן עד היכן עלה אחר כך, ויש בענין זה לדבר הרבה איך גם קדם ארץ ישראל היה חדוש נפלא כשידע מהעשרים וארבעה מיני פדיונות, או מענין ארץ ישראל הנ"ל כמו שהיה יודע אז, אך אף על פי כן נגד הידיעה שידע אחר כך ענינים אלו בעצמם כמו שידעם אחר כך אין הידיעה הראשונה נחשבת לכלום, כפי אשר הבנתי מדעתו הקדושה אך בכל ענין זה אין כלי הכתיבה מספיקים להסביר הענין היטב, והמשכילים יבינו מעט מאליהם:

en: And from this you can understand a little of a fraction of his greatness, for even earlier he was a wondrous novelty, chad bedara (one in a generation), for he said that only one in a generation knows of these twenty-four pidyonos. And all this was before the Land of Israel, and afterward, when he came from the Land of Israel, he said that he was ashamed of all the Torah teachings and attainments that he had attained before he was in the Land of Israel, and they counted for nothing in his eyes. See and understand how far he ascended afterward, and there is much to say about this matter: how even before the Land of Israel he was a wondrous novelty when he knew of the twenty-four kinds of pidyonos, or of the aforementioned matter of the Land of Israel as he knew it then; but nevertheless, compared with the knowledge by which he afterward knew these very matters, as he knew them afterward, the earlier knowledge counts for nothing, according to what I understood from his holy mind. But in this entire matter the instruments of writing are insufficient to explain the matter well, and the discerning will understand a little on their own:

translationSourceEnglish: And from this you can understand a little of a fraction of his greatness. For even before [his journey to the Land of Israel] he was already an unprecedented wondrous novelty — for he said that of these twenty-four types of pidyonos, he knew only that which is known once in a generation (chad b'dara). And all this was before the Land of Israel. And afterwards when he returned from the Land of Israel, he said that he was ashamed of all the Torahs and attainments he had attained before being in the Land of Israel, and they were as nothing in his eyes. See and understand how high he rose afterwards — and there is much to say about this matter: how even before the Land of Israel he was an unprecedented wondrous novelty when he knew the twenty-four types of pidyonos, or the matter of the Land of Israel as he knew it then. Yet even still, against the knowledge with which he afterwards knew those very same matters — as he knew them afterwards — the earlier knowledge was as nothing, as I have understood from his holy mind. But in all this matter, writing instruments are insufficient to explain the matter well, and the discerning ones will understand a little of themselves.

he: (נו) ראה זה מצאתי מכתב יד רבנו זכרונו לברכה בעצמו מענין התורה ויבן לו בית בסימן רס"ו דע כשהעולם פוגמין במצות סכה כשאין מקימין אותה כראוי גורמין מיתה או חולאת לבהמות ולשאר בעלי חיים הכל לפי הפגם. כי זה ההפרש שבין בני האדם ובין בעלי חיים כי שפעם של בני אדם יונקים ממקום בינה, כמאמר חכמינו זכרונם לברכה (ברכות י): שעשה לה דדים במקום בינה, מה שאין כן בעלי חיים, ששפעם יונקים ממקום הערוה. ובחינת סכה היא בחינת אמא בינה דמסככא על בנהא ואנו יונקים ממנה, ובזאת המצוה אנו מבדלים משפע של בעלי חיים. וכשפוגמין במצות סכה אזי יורדין על ידי זה ממדרגת בני אדם, ואין להם שפע ממקום בינה, ויורדין למדרגות שאר בעלי חיים. ונדחין שאר בעלי חיים מהשפע שלהם, כיון שבני אדם לוקחין השפע שלהם, ואזי הבעלי החיים מתים או נופלים בחלאים הכל לפי לקיחת השפע שלהם אם רב אם מעט, וזהו (בראשית ל"ג) ולמקנהו עשה סכת. הינו כי סכות הוא חיים וקיום לבעלי חיים שישארו על מדרגתם כנ"ל. וכשבני אדם יושבים בסכות כראוי, על ידי זה הם במדרגתן, ובבחינת תורה. כי התורה היא בחינת (משלי א): "אל תטש תורת אמך", "אם לבינה תקרא". (שם ב) בשביל זה סמוך לסכות אנו עושים שמחת תורה. וזה סוון ראשי תבות ו'יעקב נ'סע ס'כותה ו'יבן כי בסיון נתנה תורה ואנו במדרגת התורה על ידי מצות סכה כנזכר לעיל:

en: (56) See, this I found in the handwriting of our Rabbi, of blessed memory, himself, concerning the Torah ‘And he built himself a house,’ in section 266: Know: when the world blemishes the commandment of sukkah, when they do not fulfill it properly, they cause death or illness to the beasts and to the other living creatures, all according to the blemish. For this is the difference between human beings and living creatures, because human beings draw their bounty by nursing from the place of Binah (understanding), as our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Berakhot 10): that He made breasts for her in the place of Binah; not so living creatures, who draw their bounty by nursing from the place of the private parts. And the aspect of sukkah is the aspect of Imma-Binah (Mother-Binah), who shelters over her children, and we nurse from her; and through this commandment we are distinguished from the bounty of living creatures. And when they blemish the commandment of sukkah, then through this they descend from the level of human beings, and they have no bounty from the place of Binah, and they descend to the levels of the other living creatures. And the other living creatures are thrust away from their bounty, since human beings take their bounty; and then the living creatures die or fall into illnesses, all according to the taking of their bounty, whether much or little. And this is (Genesis 33): ‘And for his livestock he made sukkos (booths).’ That is, sukkos is life and continued existence for living creatures, so that they remain at their level, as mentioned above. And when human beings sit in sukkos properly, through this they are at their level and in the aspect of Torah. For the Torah is the aspect of (Proverbs 1): ‘Do not forsake the Torah of your mother’; ‘If you call to Binah’ (ibid. 2). For this reason, close to Sukkos we celebrate Simchas Torah. And this is ‘סוון’ (Sivan), the initial letters of ו'יעקב נ'סע ס'כותה ו'יבן (‘And Jacob journeyed to Sukkos and built’), for in Sivan the Torah was given, and we are at the level of the Torah through the commandment of sukkah, as mentioned above:

translationSourceEnglish: (56.) See this — I found in the handwriting of Rabbainu o.b.m. himself, regarding the Torah "And he built him a house" (Likutay Moharan, Torah 266): Know — when the world blemishes the mitzvah of Sukkah, when they do not fulfill it as is proper, they cause death or illness to the animals and other living creatures — everything according to the blemish. For this is the difference between human beings and other living creatures: the bounty of human beings is drawn from the place of [the Sefirah of] Binah, as our Sages of blessed memory said [Brachos 10]: that He made breasts for her in the place of Binah — which is not the case with other living creatures, whose bounty is drawn from the place of the private parts. And the aspect of Sukkah is the aspect of mother (Binah) who covers (d'mesakekhah) her children, and we draw from her — and through this mitzvah we are distinguished from the bounty of other living creatures. And when one blemishes the mitzvah of Sukkah, one then descends through this from the level of humans, and there is no bounty for them from the place of Binah, and they descend to the levels of other living creatures. And the other living creatures are displaced from their bounty, since the humans take their bounty — and then the living creatures die or fall ill — everything according to how much bounty was taken from them, whether much or little. And this is [Genesis 33:17]: "And for his cattle he built booths (sukkos)" — that is, for Sukkos is life and sustenance for the living creatures, that they remain on their level as mentioned above. And when humans sit in the Sukkos properly, through this they are on their level, and in the aspect of Torah. For the Torah is the aspect of [Proverbs 1:8]: "Do not forsake the Torah of your mother (imekha)," [Proverbs 2:3]: "If you call to Binah." Because of this, adjacent to Sukkos we celebrate Simchat Torah [the rejoicing with the Torah]. And this [is the acronym]: vayaakov nasa Sukkosah vaYiven — the initial letters: Sivan — for in Sivan the Torah was given, and we are on the level of the Torah through the mitzvah of Sukkah as mentioned above.

en: (57) Know that through the commandments of sukkah, properly [fulfilled], it is permitted for him to engage in building, and it does not harm his money; for our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Yevamot 93): One who engages in building becomes impoverished. And the reason for the matter—for what connection does poverty have with the builder? But the reason for the matter is that one who builds a building needs to build with wisdom, as it is written (Proverbs 24): ‘With wisdom a house shall be built.’ And certainly one who builds with wisdom will not become impoverished; on the contrary, he will become wealthy, and it will be fulfilled in him: ‘With wisdom a house shall be built,’ etc., ‘and with knowledge the chambers shall be filled.’ But one who builds without wisdom—they punish him with poverty, and through this his wisdom will be despised, in the aspect of (Ecclesiastes 9): ‘The wisdom of the poor man is despised,’ measure for measure. And through the commandments of sukkah he is at the level of Torah, as mentioned above, and the Torah is the source of all wisdoms. For this reason it is permitted for him to build, for certainly he has wisdom. And a sign for the matter: ‘And Jacob journeyed to Sukkos and built’—through the commandments of sukkah he was permitted to build. Lev (heart) is the initial letters of ל'ו ב'ית, lo bayis (‘for himself a house’). Lev is the Torah: bet from ‘Bereshis’ (‘In the beginning’), lamed from ‘le-einei kol Yisrael’ (‘before the eyes of all Israel’), that is, the entirety of the Torah, etc.:

translationSourceEnglish: (57.) Know — through the mitzvah of Sukkah as is proper, it is permitted for him to engage in construction and it does not harm his money, for our Rabbis of blessed memory said [Yevamos 63]: "One who engages in building becomes impoverished." And the rationale of the matter: what does poverty have to do with building? But the rationale of the matter is: one who builds a structure needs to build with wisdom, as it is written [Proverbs 24:3]: "With wisdom a house is built" — and certainly one who builds with wisdom will not become impoverished, and on the contrary, will become wealthy, and the verse [ibid.] will be fulfilled in him: "With wisdom a house is built ... and with knowledge the chambers are filled." But one who builds without wisdom is punished with poverty, and through this his wisdom is despised, in the aspect of [Ecclesiastes 9:16]: "the wisdom of the poor man is despised" — measure for measure. And through the mitzvah of Sukkah he is on the level of Torah as mentioned above, and the Torah is the source of all wisdoms — therefore it is permitted for him to build, for certainly he has wisdom. And the sign of the matter: "And Jacob traveled to Sukkos and built" — the initial letters of lo vaYiven ["lev" = heart] — heart [is] Torah. The letter lamed [comes] from "before the eyes of all Israel" [the end of the Torah]; the mem from "in the beginning" [the beginning of the Torah] — that is, the entirety of the Torah etc.

he: בדרך שאל האיש השליח להבעל שם טוב זכרונו לברכה, איך ששמעתי מכם שכשאדם עושה תשובה שלמה בודאי לא ימות קדם זמנו. וזה האיש החולה כמדמה שעשה תשובה שלמה באמת והוא איש כשר באמת, ועדין לא בא בימים כל כך, ומפני מה לא יתרפא מחליו. השיב הבעל שם טוב זכרונו לברכה להשליח אמת כך אמרתי ובודאי כן הוא וזה האיש החולה הנ"ל גם כן עשה תשובה שלמה באמת על כל חטאיו. וזה שלא נתרפא עדין הוא מחמת שלא התודה חטאיו לפני צדיק אמתי וזה שאני נוסע אליו בכדי שיתודה, ובאם שיתודה לפני תכף יתרפא, ובאם שלא ירצה להתודות לפני תכף יכבד עליו חליו ויתחיל לצעק אוי ואבוי על כל איבריו וידיו ורגליו וימות.

en: On the way, the man, the messenger, asked the Baal Shem Tov, of blessed memory: How [is this]? I heard from you that when a person performs complete repentance, certainly he will not die before his time. And this sick man, it seems, has performed complete repentance in truth, and he is an upright man in truth, and he is not yet so advanced in years; why does he not recover from his illness? The Baal Shem Tov, of blessed memory, answered the messenger: True, thus I said, and certainly it is so; and this aforementioned sick man has also performed complete repentance in truth for all his sins. And his not yet having recovered is because he has not confessed his sins before a true tzaddik; and this is why I am traveling to him, so that he may confess. And if he confesses before me, he will recover immediately; and if he does not wish to confess before me, immediately his illness will grow heavier upon him, and he will begin to cry ‘Woe and alas’ over all his limbs and his hands and his feet, and he will die.

he: וכן הוה שבא אליו הבעל שם טוב זכרונו לברכה ואמר להחולה בזה הלשון אמר מה שאתה יודע, והקדוש ברוך הוא יודע ואני יודע גם כן, הינו שיתודה לפניו כל החטאים. ואמר לו כך שלשה פעמים ולא רצה לומר. ותכף התחיל לצעק אוי ואבוי על גדל כאב כל איבריו וצעק בתמרורים בפרוטרוט על כאב כל איבר ואיבר מאיבריו, כי התחילו להשבר שקורין ברעכין כל עצמותיו של כל איבר ואיבר, וצעק כך מתוך חליו איזה זמן עד שמת כמו שאמר הבעל שם טוב זכרונו לברכה.
he_nikud: וְכֵן הֲוָה שֶׁבָּא אֵלָיו הַבַּעַל־שֵׁם־טוֹב זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה וְאָמַר לְהַחוֹלֶה בְּזֶה הַלָּשׁוֹן אֱמֹר מַה שֶּׁאַתָּה יוֹדֵעַ, וְהַקָּדוֹשׁ־בָּרוּךְ־הוּא יוֹדֵעַ וַאֲנִי יוֹדֵעַ גַּם־כֵּן, הַיְנוּ שֶׁיִּתְוַדֶּה לְפָנָיו כָּל הַחֲטָאִים. וְאָמַר לוֹ כָּךְ שְׁלשָׁה פְּעָמִים וְלֹא רָצָה לוֹמַר. וְתֵכֶף הִתְחִיל לִצְעֹק אוֹי וַאֲבוֹי עַל גֹּדֶל כְּאֵב כָּל אֵיבָרָיו וְצָעַק בְּתַמְרוּרִים בִּפְרוֹטְרוֹט עַל כְּאֵב כָּל אֵיבָר וְאֵיבָר מֵאֵיבָרָיו, כִּי הִתְחִילוּ לְהִשָּׁבֵר שֶׁקּוֹרִין בְּרֶעכִין כָּל עַצְמוֹתָיו שֶׁל כָּל אֵיבָר וְאֵיבָר, וְצָעַק כָּךְ מִתּוֹךְ חָלְיוֹ אֵיזֶה זְמַן עַד שֶׁמֵּת כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר הַבַּעַל־שֵׁם־טוֹב זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה.
en: And so it was: the Baal Shem Tov, of blessed memory, came to him and said to the sick man in these words: ‘Say what you know, and the Holy One, blessed be He, knows, and I too know’—that is, that he should confess before him all the sins. And he said this to him three times, and [the sick man] did not wish to say [it]. And immediately he began to cry ‘Woe and alas’ over the great pain of all his limbs, and cried bitterly, in detail, over the pain of each and every one of his limbs, for all his bones of each and every limb began to break, which they call brekhin; and he cried thus in the midst of his illness for some time until he died, as the Baal Shem Tov, of blessed memory, had said.
